title: Secondary-use research in a controlled environment
recipient: University research group studying ED crowding and revisits
purpose: Analyse length of stay, revisits and diagnosis patterns
threat_model: Researcher with access to public_directory, news_clips_health and social_posts_health; may try record linkage on QIs (age, sex, municipality, arrival time).
legal_context: Pseudonymised data remains personal data (GDPR Recital 26); health data is Art. 9 special category. Comparable to a permit-based secure processing environment.
suggested_privacy_targets: No direct identifiers; consistent pseudonymous patient key; QIs generalised so that k>=5 on (age band, sex, municipality, arrival week); free text redacted (recall >=0.95 on PERSON/PHONE/ADDRESS/NATIONAL_ID).
notes: Revisit analysis needs a stable patient pseudonym and joinable visit/lab keys.

title: Public weekly dashboard
purpose: Weekly ED load, influenza-like illness and injury trends by age band and municipality
threat_model: Any outsider with news clips, social posts and the public directory; can download every weekly release and difference them.
legal_context: Must be anonymous in the GDPR sense (not reasonably re-identifiable). Small cells and repeated releases are the main risk.
suggested_privacy_targets: Aggregate only; differential privacy with a stated mechanism and ε (e.g. ε<=1 per weekly release, documented composition) or suppression of cells <5 with complementary suppression.
notes: Compare against data/health/published_weekly_stats.csv, which is an example of what NOT to publish.

title: AI vendor training a triage-support model
recipient: External AI vendor under a data-processing agreement
purpose: Train a model predicting admission from triage-time information
threat_model: Vendor staff or a breach; membership inference on synthetic data; memorised rare patients.
legal_context: Processor relationship; data minimisation; synthetic data must not reproduce real records (check distance to closest record and membership inference).
suggested_privacy_targets: Fully synthetic or strongly generalised training table without free text; membership-inference AUC close to 0.5 against holdout; no record closer to a real one than real records are to each other.
notes: Use holdout/health as non-members for membership-inference tests.

title: Open data: public-transport origin-destination matrices
recipient: Anyone (municipal open data portal, CC BY 4.0)
purpose: Publish weekly OD flows between areas by hour band for journey planners, researchers and citizens.
threat_model: Any outsider with public_directory, social_checkins and fitness_app_leak; can see a neighbour at a stop.
legal_context: Only anonymous data may be published openly (GDPR Recital 26). Pseudonymised card ids are personal data.
suggested_privacy_targets: No row-level data; no card ids; suppress or noise OD cells < 10 trips; consider ε-DP counts per release.
notes: Taps are boardings only; destinations require trip chaining before aggregation.

title: Urban planning consultancy: row-level journeys under contract
recipient: Planning consultancy (processor under a data processing agreement)
purpose: Redesign of the bus network: transfers, commuting corridors, peak loads.
threat_model: Curious analyst with public_directory + social_checkins; must not be able to single out riders.
legal_context: Pseudonymised data is still personal data; data minimisation and purpose limitation apply (GDPR Art. 5, 28).
suggested_privacy_targets: Keyed (HMAC) card pseudonyms rotated per week; no holder fields; times rounded to 5-15 min; trajectory unicity < 5 % with 4 known points.
notes: Linking trips of the same card within a day is needed for transfers; across weeks it mostly adds risk.

title: Academic research on mobility and bikes
purpose: Study mode choice between bus and city bike, weather effects, commuting distances.
threat_model: Researcher with all public adversary files; private evaluation adds colleague knowledge (employer + arrival time).
legal_context: Scientific research safeguards (GDPR Art. 89); pseudonymisation expected; publication of results must be anonymous.
suggested_privacy_targets: No email-like accounts; GPS start/end snapped to ≥250 m grid or zones; k ≥ 5 on (home area, work area, card type).
notes: Bike GPS end points near homes are the main re-identification risk.

title: Open data: city-centre footfall
purpose: Publish hourly footfall by zone for businesses, events and citizens.
threat_model: Outsider with public plate_sightings and knowledge of when a neighbour walks home.
legal_context: MAC addresses are personal data (online identifiers, GDPR Recital 30); only anonymous aggregates can be open data.
suggested_privacy_targets: Hourly zone-level counts only; suppress or noise counts < 5 (night-time); no MACs, no SSIDs.
notes: Counting distinct randomised MACs over-counts people; say so in the release notes.

title: Share with the city-centre retail association
purpose: Dwell time, repeat visits, Black Friday and Christmas market effects, parking demand.
threat_model: Association member with its own loyalty-app device list (private adversary) and plate sightings.
legal_context: Re-identifying visitors for marketing would need a new lawful basis; minimise and pseudonymise (GDPR Art. 5, 6, 25).
suggested_privacy_targets: Daily-rotating keyed pseudonyms for MACs and plates; drop SSIDs and payment fields; coarsen times to 15 min.
notes: Repeat-visitor share needs linkage across days; consider computing it inside the controller and sharing the result.

title: Request from police / parking enforcement
purpose: A request for all plates and payment details at P-Riverside over two weeks, 'for an investigation'.
threat_model: Function creep: data collected for parking fees reused for surveillance.
legal_context: Purpose limitation (GDPR Art. 5(1)(b)); disclosures to authorities need a specific legal basis and are assessed case by case (Law Enforcement Directive). Not legal advice.
suggested_privacy_targets: Show what a minimal, case-specific disclosure would contain versus the bulk request; log the disclosure.
notes: A good demo explains why the PET answer here is mostly 'share less', not 'transform more'.

title: Open data: neighbourhood electricity load
purpose: Urban energy planning, journalism, research on heating transition.
threat_model: Public: vacation_posts + public_directory; neighbours who know their own consumption (differencing).
legal_context: Only anonymous information may be published; aggregated small areas with few households can still be personal data.
suggested_privacy_targets: Aggregate ≥10 metering points per cell; no individual series; consider DP noise on hourly sums (state ε).
notes: Weather table is public context.

title: Row-level hourly data to a flexibility aggregator
purpose: Identify flexible loads (heat pumps, EV) and forecast them.
threat_model: Curious insider at the recipient with public_directory and vacation_posts; private: neighbour_knowledge.
legal_context: Pseudonymised personal data (GDPR Art. 4(5)); minimisation and purpose limitation apply.
suggested_privacy_targets: No names/addresses/contacts; keyed pseudonym for metering point; generalise location to ≥3-digit postcode; coarsen or suppress rare attributes; assess absence inference.
notes: Series must remain linkable over time for forecasting.

title: Energy-poverty research dataset
purpose: Relate heating type, payment problems and winter consumption.
threat_model: Researcher with public_directory; private: broker_profiles.
legal_context: Scientific research (GDPR Art. 89) with safeguards; health flag needs special care (Art. 9).
suggested_privacy_targets: k≥5 on {postcode area, heating_type, floor area band, ev, solar}; remove or noise medical flag; daily rather than hourly values may suffice.

title: Cross-bank fraud consortium
recipient: Fraud data-sharing consortium of several banks
purpose: Pool card transactions to detect fraud patterns that span banks.
threat_model: Consortium member analyst with receipt_photos_ocr and public_directory; private: merchant_knowledge.
legal_context: Fraud prevention as legitimate interest (GDPR Art. 6(1)(f), Recital 47); pseudonymised data; PCI DSS for PANs.
suggested_privacy_targets: Keyed tokens (HMAC with consortium key) for PAN/device/IP so the same card links across banks; drop names/contacts; coarsen time to minute; no raw PAN.
notes: Linkability across banks is the point — random tokens destroy it.

title: External AI vendor builds a fraud / spending model
purpose: Train and evaluate a fraud model and a spending-category model.
threat_model: Vendor staff with public receipts and directory; private: merchant_knowledge, broker_profiles.
legal_context: Processor under Art. 28; minimisation; special-category inferences must not be exposed.
suggested_privacy_targets: No direct identifiers; tokenised card; generalise merchant to MCC group for sensitive MCCs; k-anonymity on customer profile; consider synthetic data with DCR/MIA checks.

title: Statistics office: consumer spending statistics
purpose: Monthly spending by category and region; payday and seasonal effects.
threat_model: Anyone with public receipts; differencing between releases.
legal_context: Published outputs must be anonymous.
suggested_privacy_targets: Aggregate tables with ≥10 cardholders per cell; dominance rule for merchants; DP noise on sums (state ε and clipping bound).

title: Outsource 24/7 monitoring to an external MSSP
recipient: Managed security service provider under a data processing agreement
purpose: Detect and investigate threats across sign-in, VPN, proxy, DNS, EDR and e-mail telemetry
threat_model: Curious MSSP analyst with company_website_staff.csv (public) and general OSINT; may try to learn who is who or what employees browse.
legal_context: Processor under GDPR Art. 28; pseudonymised data is still personal data. Employee monitoring must be proportionate (in Finland, the Act on the Protection of Privacy in Working Life).
suggested_privacy_targets: Keyed (HMAC) pseudonyms for users, hosts and internal IPs, consistent across all tables; secrets and e-mails removed from URLs and command lines; sensitive web categories generalised; re-identification only by the company holding the key.
notes: Random per-row tokens look safer but make every cross-log detection impossible.

title: Share indicators with the national CERT / sector ISAC
recipient: National CERT and other logistics companies (threat-intelligence sharing community)
purpose: Share attacker infrastructure and TTPs from campaigns C1 and C2 so others can block them
threat_model: Other community members are competitors; anything about Meridian staff, customers or internal network layout is out of scope.
legal_context: Legitimate interest in network security (GDPR Recital 49); share the minimum necessary.
suggested_privacy_targets: Only external attacker IoCs (IPs, domains, user agents, hashes, techniques, timestamps); no employee identifiers, no internal IPs or hostnames, victim count only as aggregate.
notes: Attacker IPs are not personal data of employees and must stay exact - masking them destroys the value.

title: Publish an open research dataset for detection research
purpose: Benchmark for detection of phishing chains, spraying and insider exfiltration
threat_model: Motivated outsider with company_website_staff.csv and breach/OSINT data (private broker file used in evaluation) trying to identify employees, their browsing, sick leaves or the insider.
legal_context: Must be anonymous in the GDPR Recital 26 sense: no means reasonably likely to re-identify.
suggested_privacy_targets: No direct identifiers or secrets; prefix-preserving IP anonymisation with a discarded key; time-shifted or coarsened timestamps; sensitive categories and subjects removed; check that no employee is unique on (department, job_title, site, shift); e-mail subjects and ticket text removed or fully redacted.
notes: Labelled campaigns must stay detectable after protection.

title: Statistics publication for the education authority
purpose: Publish grade, completion and drop-out statistics by school, programme, sex and language group.
threat_model: Anyone, with graduation lists and sports rosters (public adversary files); differencing between tables.
legal_context: Output must be anonymous (GDPR Recital 26). Traditional practice is suppressing cells with n<5; compare with differential privacy.
suggested_privacy_targets: No cell below 5 unless noise-protected; no microdata; state ε if DP is used; consistent totals across tables.
notes: Small schools and programmes are the hard part.

title: Ed-tech vendor training a drop-out early-warning model
recipient: External ed-tech company under a data processing agreement
purpose: Train a model that predicts drop-out risk from grades and absences.
threat_model: Vendor staff with classmate-level knowledge (private adversary) and public lists.
legal_context: Pseudonymised data is still personal data; minimise fields; special categories (religion, health) need a separate legal basis.
suggested_privacy_targets: No direct identifiers or free text; religion/S2/support removed or justified; k>=5 on (school, programme, start year, sex, birth year).
notes: Keyed pseudonyms must keep the student_id join across tables.

title: Researcher studying grade gaps
recipient: University research group in a controlled environment
purpose: Analyse gender and language-group gaps in maths and matriculation results.
threat_model: Researcher with access to public lists; risk of spontaneous recognition in small schools.
legal_context: Scientific research (GDPR Art. 89) with safeguards; pseudonymisation and data minimisation expected.
suggested_privacy_targets: k>=10 on quasi-identifiers or synthetic microdata with documented fidelity; no notes text.

title: Open data publication of citizen feedback
purpose: Publish requests with category, time, area, status and the text so residents and journalists can follow service quality.
threat_model: Anyone: neighbours, forum users (public adversary: neighbourhood_forum_posts), permit registry (public).
legal_context: Published data must be anonymous; free text needs redaction of all personal data including third parties.
suggested_privacy_targets: No direct identifiers in any column or text; locations coarsened (e.g. 250 m grid or street level without house numbers); time to the hour or day; no account ids.
notes: Several cities publish feedback like this. The text is where most of the value and most of the risk is.

title: Internal analytics team
purpose: Dashboards on workload, response times and repeat issues.
threat_model: Curious colleague with insider knowledge (private adversary).
legal_context: Same controller; data minimisation and pseudonymisation still expected (GDPR Art. 5, 25).
suggested_privacy_targets: Keyed pseudonyms for reporters (stable, so repeat reporting can be analysed); no contact details; text redacted.

title: Research group studying service equity
purpose: Do response times differ between areas and languages?
threat_model: Researchers with public data (forum, permits).
legal_context: Research use (GDPR Art. 89) with a data use agreement.
suggested_privacy_targets: k>=5 on (postcode, category, month, language); no text or redacted text; aggregated reporter activity.

title: Transcripts to an external LLM analytics vendor
recipient: Cloud AI vendor (processor, outside the EU possible)
purpose: Topic mining, contact-reason trends and agent-quality insights on all channels.
threat_model: Vendor staff and model logs see all text; insider can link with leaked_customer_list.csv (public) or breach dumps (private evaluation).
legal_context: Processor under GDPR Art. 28; transfer safeguards if outside EEA. Pseudonymised text is still personal data; aim for no direct identifiers and no special-category data in text.
suggested_privacy_targets: No residual direct identifiers in text (recall ≥ 0.98 on NATIONAL_ID, PAYMENT_CARD, IBAN, SECRET); remove HEALTH mentions; consistent pseudonyms within a conversation; round timestamps to the hour.
notes: Keep the intent signal: do not delete whole utterances.

title: Train an internal intent model / chatbot
purpose: Train an intent classifier and response suggestions.
threat_model: Model memorisation: verbatim identifiers in training text can be regurgitated by a generative model.
legal_context: Compatible further processing (Art. 6(4)); data minimisation (Art. 5(1)(c)).
suggested_privacy_targets: Replace identifiers with typed placeholders or realistic surrogates; no secrets or card numbers anywhere; free text k-anonymised for rare phrases optional.
notes: Surrogates (fake names) preserve fluency better than [REDACTED].

title: Quality-audit samples to an outsourced BPO
purpose: Score 500 conversations a month for compliance (identity verification done, card numbers refused).
threat_model: Auditors are human readers; re-identification by recognising neighbours or public figures; linkage via customer_id and timestamps.
legal_context: Processor; access limited to sample; retention 90 days.
suggested_privacy_targets: Mask identifiers but keep evidence that verification happened (e.g. '[NATIONAL_ID]' placeholder); drop customer_id; generalise started_ts to week.
notes: Auditor must still see that the agent stopped a card number being read out.
